restored_passages.before: Figure~\ref{fig:vgg_saliency_comparison_main} compares split and baseline saliency maps at their best-performing layers. Mid-layer SplitCAM resembles earlier-layer classical $\gamma$-\ac{lrp}. Against same-layer LayerCAM, it gives more weight across object pixels while emphasizing key features, balancing interpretability and focus (low entropy). For $\alpha \ll 0.5$, SplitGrad yields less focused, finely aligned gradients following image details. We attribute this to Maxout retaining pre-activation information that ReLU discards at inactive neurons. Further examples appear in Section~\ref{app:saliency}.
restored_passages.after: Figure~\ref{fig:vgg_saliency_comparison_main} qualitatively compares saliency maps from our split methods with their baseline counterparts at the best-performing layers. Mid-layer SplitCAM shares key visual characteristics with classical $\gamma$-\ac{lrp} from earlier layers. Compared to standard LayerCAM on the same layer it focuses more weight to all object pixels, while still marking the key object features as especially important. For $\alpha \ll 0.5$, SplitGrad yields less focused yet finely aligned gradients that closely follow image details. We attribute this to the Maxout activation retaining preactivation information, unlike ReLU, which discards it in inactive neurons. Overall, mid-layer SplitCAM offers an effective balance between interpretability and focus (low entropy).

restored_passages.before: \textbf{Gradient} is raw input-gradient saliency~\parencite{Simonyan2014}: the maximum absolute gradient over color channels. \textbf{SmGrad} averages noisy gradient maps (SmoothGrad)~\parencite{Smilkov2017}. \textbf{IntGrad} uses Integrated Gradients~\parencite{Sundararajan2017} with a black-image baseline. \textbf{DeepLIFT} propagates activation differences from a reference input using the Rescale rule~\parencite{Shrikumar2017} (CNNs only). \textbf{DAVE} is the distribution-aware ViT gradient decomposition of \textcite{Wrobel2024}; our implementation additionally freezes the LayerNorm mean, whereas published DAVE differentiates through mean-centering. \textbf{SG}, our \ac{sg}, belongs here because its occupation measure recovers the gradient (Theorem~\ref{ptnb:thm:deriv-occ}).
restored_passages.after: \textbf{Gradient} is the raw input-gradient saliency map~\parencite{Simonyan2014}, the maximum over color channels of the absolute gradient. \textbf{SmGrad} is SmoothGrad, i.e.\ an average over noisy gradient maps~\parencite{Smilkov2017}. \textbf{IntGrad} is Integrated Gradients~\parencite{Sundararajan2017} with a black-image baseline. \textbf{DeepLIFT} propagates activation differences relative to a reference input with the Rescale rule~\parencite{Shrikumar2017} (CNNs only). \textbf{DAVE} is the distribution-aware ViT gradient decomposition of~\textcite{Wrobel2024}; our implementation additionally freezes the LayerNorm mean, whereas published DAVE differentiates through mean-centering. \textbf{SG} is our \ac{sg}, included in this block because it recovers the gradient as a Stopping-Game occupation measure (Theorem~\ref{ptnb:thm:deriv-occ}).
restored_passages.qualification: Preserve exact DAVE implementation qualification and current checked citation keys.

restored_passages.before: \textbf{LRP-$\varepsilon$} is stabilized Layer-wise Relevance Propagation~\parencite{Bach2015}; \textbf{LRP-$\gamma$} amplifies positive weights~\parencite{Montavon_2022_gammaLRP}. \textbf{AttnLRP} propagates transformer relevance through softmax, the bilinear attention product and the Value path~\parencite{Achtibat2024AttnLRP}. \textbf{RG} is our \ac{rg}; \textbf{RG+Eq} adds equivariant Reynolds averaging, mainly to suppress ViT tokenization-grid artifacts. \textbf{TIBAV}~\parencite{Chefer2021GenericAttention}, \textbf{GAE}~\parencite{Chefer2021ICCV} and Attention Rollout (\textbf{AR}) are transformer attention-map baselines.
restored_passages.after: \textbf{LRP-$\varepsilon$} denotes the stabilized Layer-wise Relevance Propagation rule~\parencite{Bach2015}. \textbf{LRP-$\gamma$} is the positive-weight-amplified LRP variant~\parencite{Montavon_2022_gammaLRP}. \textbf{AttnLRP} is transformer LRP that propagates relevance through the softmax and the bilinear attention product as well as the Value path~\parencite{Achtibat2024AttnLRP}. \textbf{RG} is our \ac{rg}. \textbf{RG+Eq} is the same method with equivariant Reynolds averaging, used mainly on ViT to suppress tokenization-grid artifacts. \textbf{TIBAV}~\parencite{Chefer2021GenericAttention}, \textbf{GAE}~\parencite{Chefer2021ICCV} and Attention Rollout (\textbf{AR}) are the transformer-specific attention-map baselines.
